name: Michelle Xia
current_role: Co-founder, Chairwoman, President and CEO, Akeso Inc. (HKEX: 9926)
profile: Biochemist (Sun Yat-sen University) who spent ~12 years in U.S. research and biotech (University of Louisville, Bayer, Crown Bioscience) before returning to China in 2008 and co-founding Akeso in 2012. Akeso's PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab, licensed to Summit Therapeutics in 2022, beat Merck's Keytruda in a 2024 Phase 3 trial.
interesting_fact: Akeso's ivonescimab outperformed Merck's blockbuster Keytruda in a head-to-head Phase 3 lung cancer trial in 2024; Summit Therapeutics paid $500M upfront (up to $5B in milestones) for rights in the U.S., Europe and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech she earned postgraduate degrees at Newcastle and Glasgow universities in the UK, then moved to the U.S. in 1996 to do cancer immunotherapy research at the University of Louisville. Akeso is named after the Greek goddess of healing.
notes: Company site only; no published press/IR email found on akesobio.com. Akeso press releases go out via PR Newswire. She also sits on Summit Therapeutics' board (smmttx.com).

name: Ali Erdemoglu
current_role: Board chairman/deputy chairman of Merinos Halı and vice chairman of SASA Polyester (Erdemoğlu Holding); sources differ on current Merinos title
profile: Co-owner with brother İbrahim of Erdemoğlu Holding (Gaziantep), which grew from father Mehmet's two looms in 1970 into Merinos and Dinarsu carpets, among the world's largest carpet makers. In 2015 the brothers bought 51% of SASA Polyester for $102M and now own over 75%. SASA is expanding into petrochemicals, including a planned $25B Yumurtalık complex.
interesting_fact: He started in the carpet trade with his father right after primary school; SASA has a $935M licensing and technical-service agreement with Koch Industries' Invista.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 he accepted first prize (large-company category) in Turkey's Industrial Energy Efficiency Awards at the 2nd National Energy Summit in Gaziantep. Merinos won for upgrading compressors and electric motors in its factories, a natural hook for an energy podcast.
notes: Both are general group inboxes (Erdemoğlu Holding, SASA). Brother İbrahim chairs the holding and is its more public face. Turkish-language outreach is likely more effective.

name: Jorge Pinheiro Koren de Lima
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Hapvida (Hapvida NotreDame Intermédica); stepped down as CEO in 2026 after ~25 years, succeeded by Luccas Adib
profile: Fortaleza-born physician (Federal University of Ceará), elder son of oncologist Candido Pinheiro, who founded Hapvida. He ran Hapvida as CEO from 2001, taking it public in 2018 and merging it with NotreDame Intermédica into one of Brazil's largest vertically integrated health insurers. In 2026 he handed the CEO role to CFO Luccas Adib and became board chairman.
interesting_fact: Hapvida's vertical model pairs health insurance with its own hospitals and clinics. At its 2018 IPO it had 47 hospitals and nearly 200 clinics, and the 2022 NotreDame Intermédica merger made it a national giant.
notes: CEO succession was announced Dec 2025 and took effect around Apr 30, 2026 (suno.com.br, brapi.dev). Sources differ on the founding year: Forbes says 1986, others say 1979 (Hospital Antônio Prudente, Fortaleza). Low public profile; IR form is the main route. No sourced personal deep-cut found.

name: Mai Gang
current_role: Angel investor and founder of 创业工场 (Chuangye Gongchang); early Pop Mart shareholder
profile: Chinese angel investor who in August 2012 became Pop Mart's first institutional backer, putting in RMB 2M at a RMB 12.5M valuation. Reports say he still held 44M+ Pop Mart shares in 2025, and its rise made him a Hurun-listed rich lister (listed jointly with Mai Haoyun). He was also an early Chinese bitcoin evangelist and mentored OKX founder Xu Mingxing.
interesting_fact: He reportedly decided to back Pop Mart within days of meeting founder Wang Ning, while it was a small Beijing apartment operation. Reports describe the stake's return as over a thousandfold.
deep_cut_fact: Wang Ning has credited Mai Gang with writing Pop Mart's early slogan, 想泡就泡，管它玛特 (roughly 'Pop in whenever you like, never mind the mart'). He was also investing pocket money in bitcoin before finishing university and promoted it nationwide in 2013.
notes: Also romanised as Gang Mai / Michael Mai. He invested in Xu Mingxing's Docin.com and was involved in founding OKCoin (chaincatcher.com/en/article/2187116). No verified official site or social accounts found; he has appeared on the Xiaoyuzhou FM podcast (crypto.news, Jul 2025). Relationship to Mai Haoyun not established.

name: Gao Lufeng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Segway-Ninebot (九号公司, SSE STAR: 689009)
profile: Beihang University engineering graduate who co-founded Ninebot with fellow alumnus Wang Ye in 2012 to make self-balancing scooters. In 2015, backed by Xiaomi and Sequoia, Ninebot bought its former patent rival Segway outright. Segway-Ninebot listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and now sells e-scooters, e-mopeds, robot lawnmowers and service robots.
interesting_fact: Ninebot bought Segway in April 2015, while Segway had a patent complaint pending against it. Gao said of the old rival: 'It seemed like we were facing a competitor that was tough to beat.'
deep_cut_fact: His first venture with Wang Ye, started in 2003 as he graduated from Beihang, was a smart-toy project that sold 2,000+ units before failing over quality, manufacturing and cash-flow problems. In 2009 Wang phoned him to reunite, which led to their balance-scooter business.
notes: No published IR or press email found. IR filings name board secretary Xu Peng as the investor contact (via SSE e-interaction). Strong fit for an energy/EV-mobility episode.

name: Zhou Rongrong
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director, Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨, HKEX: 2589)
profile: Co-founded tea-drink chain Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨) in 2013 with husband Shan Weijun; both left jobs at a U.S. Fortune 500 company. It started as a 25 m² shop on People's Square, Shanghai, selling purple-rice milk tea, grew to 9,000+ mostly franchised stores in lower-tier cities, and listed in Hong Kong in May 2025.
interesting_fact: The first shop sold 1,000+ cups on opening day in July 2013, with queues tens of metres long, and took over RMB 300,000 in its first month.
deep_cut_fact: The idea was hers. In 2013 she wandered into a Shanghai lane and saw a queue outside an unsigned milk-tea shop that cooked tea with blood glutinous rice. That inspired a 'Shanghai-style' milk tea, and the brand name ('Shanghai Auntie') honours the aunties who ran such lane shops.
notes: Aggregators list her as Executive Director plus Deputy CEO or Chief Product Officer (unverified); husband Shan Weijun is chairman and the main public voice. No published IR email found. Check HKEXnews filings for the company secretary contact. Originally from Shandong.

name: Michael Tabor
current_role: Racehorse owner and partner in Coolmore Stud's ownership group; private investor (hotels, property, entertainment)
profile: East London-born bookmaker who in 1968 borrowed £30,000 to buy two bankrupt betting shops, grew the Arthur Prince chain to 114 shops, and sold it to Coral in 1995 for a reported £27M. He then became a leading thoroughbred owner in partnership with Coolmore's John Magnier, and invests in hotels, property and entertainment.
interesting_fact: He is one of only four owners to have won both the Epsom Derby (Galileo 2001, High Chaparral 2002) and the Kentucky Derby (Thunder Gulch, 1995).
deep_cut_fact: He left East Ham Grammar School at 15 to work at the local Co-op and nearly became a hairdresser, enrolling at the Morris School of Hairdressing in Piccadilly, before turning to bookmaking. His first racehorse, Tornado Prince, cost £2,850 in 1973 and won seven races.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contacts found. Born 1941; no report of death found as of Wikipedia. A possible route is via Coolmore/racing circles. Favourite quote: 'good punters make good bookmakers.' Web search budget was exhausted, so research was limited to Wikipedia.

name: Edward S Hyman
current_role: Chairman of Evercore ISI; non-executive role at Evercore since Feb 2025 (formerly Vice Chairman of Evercore)
profile: Wall Street economist Ed Hyman founded the macro and equity research firm ISI (International Strategy & Investment) in 1991. Evercore bought it in 2014 (Wikipedia puts the price at ~$440M) and he became Vice Chairman of Evercore and Chairman of Evercore ISI. In Feb 2025 he moved to a non-executive role but still supports the ISI business. His wealth is mainly Evercore stock.
interesting_fact: In 2014 Evercore merged its equities unit into Ed Hyman's ISI to create Evercore ISI. At the time, 32% of ISI's analysts were ranked #1 or #2 by Institutional Investor.
notes: The role change is from an 8-K dated 2025-02-14 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1360901/000119312525027351/d828246d8k.htm). He is widely known as a long-time top-ranked economist in Institutional Investor's polls, but that was not verified here because the search budget ran out. A macro voice who fits an energy/data-center capex discussion.

name: Zhang Jiming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, West China Cement Ltd (HKEX: 2233)
profile: Zhang Jimin (张继民; romanised Jimin by the company) built West China Cement from two small township cement plants in Pucheng County, Shaanxi, which he managed from 1985. The Yaobai group listed on London's AIM in 2006 and moved to Hong Kong in 2010. Since 2020 it has expanded into sub-Saharan Africa and Central Asia, and he also chairs the Shaanxi Province Cement Association.
interesting_fact: Since 2020 West China Cement has built cement capacity in sub-Saharan Africa and Central Asia. His 2026 chairman's statement says those overseas plants now contribute significantly to profits as China's cement demand falls.
deep_cut_fact: From 1992 to 1994 he led development of low-heat slag cement and moderate-heat Portland cement. The work won a Second Grade Science and Technology Progress Prize from the Shaanxi provincial government. He began as manager of the Hanjing Town Second Cement Factory in 1985.
notes: The company spells his name Zhang Jimin; he was aged 71 per the company bio. The Africa expansion angle suits the infrastructure/energy theme. HQ is in Xi'an.

name: Song Guihua
current_role: Co-holder, with Jiang Guiting, of the controlling family stake in Jingjin Equipment Inc. (景津装备, SSE: 603279); personal title not verified
profile: Listed by Hurun together with Jiang Guiting, chairman of Jingjin Equipment, a Dezhou (Shandong) filter-press maker founded in 1988 and listed in Shanghai in October 2019. Jingjin says it has been the world's largest filter-press producer by capacity and sales for 12 straight years, selling to 123 countries. Her own role in the company could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Jingjin, the family company, is the primary drafter of China's national standards for filter presses and filter plates. Its filter presses are used for mining tailings, wastewater and palm-oil effluent across 123 countries.
notes: Search budget was exhausted, so her relationship to Jiang Guiting and her role are unverified (likely a family co-controller; check the 603279 annual report). The email is a general sales inbox on the company's English site. Chairman Jiang Guiting won a gold medal at the 68th Nuremberg International Invention Exhibition (2018).

name: Xiong Fengxiang
current_role: Co-holder, with Xiong Jun, of a founding stake in Shanghai Junshi Biosciences (君实生物, SSE: 688180 / HKEX: 1877); current title not verified
profile: Hurun lists him jointly with Xiong Jun as wealth holders in Junshi Biosciences, a Shanghai biopharma company founded in December 2012. Its lead drug, the PD-1 antibody toripalimab, was approved in China in 2018, by the U.S. FDA in October 2023 and in the EU in 2024. His personal role and background could not be verified here.
interesting_fact: Junshi's toripalimab won U.S. FDA approval in October 2023 (nasopharyngeal carcinoma) with priority review, breakthrough-therapy and orphan-drug designations, then EU authorisation in September 2024.
notes: Search budget was exhausted, so his identity and relationship to Xiong Jun (Junshi's co-founder and chairman) are unverified; check Junshi's HKEX annual report. The only email on the contact page is MI@junshipharma.com, which is for medical information, not press.

name: Xu Zhiwei
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jiangsu Longliqi Group (隆力奇), Changshu (as of 2023)
profile: Founded Longliqi in Changshu, Jiangsu in 1986. It became known for snake-oil skin cream, florida water (花露水), toiletries and health supplements. In 2012 he also launched the e-commerce platform 聚好商城 (Juhao Mall) as its CEO. Hurun China listed him from 2005 to 2017.
interesting_fact: Longliqi's best-known product is snake-oil cream (蛇油膏), a mass-market Chinese toiletry brand he built from Changshu starting in 1986.
notes: Zh Wikipedia reports that in Feb 2023 he was placed on bail by Suzhou police over alleged illegal fundraising, possibly linked to a shareholder dispute at Juhao Mall; check the current status before any outreach. No published contact email found. Search budget was exhausted, so research was limited.

name: Shrikantadevi R Damani
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder in Avenue Supermarts Ltd (DMart); no public executive role found
profile: Wife of DMart founder Radhakishan Damani. Hurun India (2017-2019) listed her for her own shareholding in Avenue Supermarts, the hypermarket chain her husband started after leaving the stock market in 2000. DMart opened its first store in Powai, Mumbai in 2002 and listed in 2017.
interesting_fact: DMart grew from a single Powai store in 2002 to 25 stores by 2010 before its blockbuster 2017 IPO.
notes: Private individual with no public profile, interviews or accounts. Any approach should go to Avenue Supermarts' company secretary/IR or to R.K. Damani; she is not a natural podcast guest. No published IR email could be retrieved because the site is JavaScript-rendered.
